\chapter{Asking Well}
\label{ch:ta-asking-well}
\hlchaptermodality{63}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can name a request, permission, hesitancy, trust and humility in Tamil.}

Complete TA-C63-humility and say all five words in order.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[vēṇḍukōḷ]{\ta{வேண்டுகோள்} (vēṇḍukōḷ) — a request}

\label{lesson:TA-C63-request}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{uṭaṉē} mean, and what did \emph{mutalil} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{வேண்டுகோள்}}
\textbf{\ta{வேண்டுகோள்}} (\emph{vēṇḍukōḷ}) — \textquotedblleft{}a request\textquotedblright{}.

A request as a thing you make and hand over, rather than the asking itself. It stands beside \ta{வேண்டும்}, which you already have, and you can hear that word at the front of it.

Kannada \ka{ವಿನಂತಿ} (\emph{vinanti}) and Telugu \te{మనవి} (\emph{manavi}) both went their own way. A \ta{வேண்டுகோள்} is what \ta{தயவுசெய்து} is put in front of when the asking has to be formal.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The first of five.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{vēṇḍukōḷ}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{vēṇḍukōḷ}, then \emph{tayavu seytu}, and say which one dresses the other
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{வேண்டுகோள்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}a request\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[aṉumati]{\ta{அனுமதி} (aṉumati) — permission}

\label{lesson:TA-C63-permission}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{vēṇḍukōḷ} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{அனுமதி}}
\textbf{\ta{அனுமதி}} (\emph{aṉumati}) — \textquotedblleft{}permission\textquotedblright{}.

Permission to do a thing — asked for, given, refused. Here all three sisters took the same Sanskrit word and did not even change its shape: Kannada \ka{ಅನುಮತಿ} (\emph{anumati}), Telugu \te{అనుమతి} (\emph{anumati}), Tamil \ta{அனுமதி}.

Hold it apart from \ta{விடை}, which you already have. \ta{விடை} is permission to go, taken formally at a door. \ta{அனுமதி} is the wider one and covers everything else you might be allowed.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Two.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{aṉumati}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{aṉumati}, then \emph{viḍai}, and say which of the two is only about leaving
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{அனுமதி} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}permission\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[tayakkam]{\ta{தயக்கம்} (tayakkam) — hesitancy}

\label{lesson:TA-C63-hesitancy}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{aṉumati} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{தயக்கம்}}
\textbf{\ta{தயக்கம்}} (\emph{tayakkam}) — \textquotedblleft{}hesitancy\textquotedblright{}.

The holding back before you ask: the half-step not taken, the sentence begun and dropped. Kannada carries the same idea in \ka{ಸಂಕೋಚ} (\emph{saṅkōca}).

The \ta{தயவு} inside \ta{தயவுசெய்து} opens the same way and is a different word — that one is kindness given, this one is a foot kept back. Tamil puts them next to each other and expects you to hear the difference.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Three.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{tayakkam}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{tayakkam}, then \emph{tayavu seytu}, and say which one is a giving
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{தயக்கம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}hesitancy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nambikkai]{\ta{நம்பிக்கை} (nambikkai) — trust}

\label{lesson:TA-C63-trust}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{tayakkam} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{நம்பிக்கை}}
\textbf{\ta{நம்பிக்கை}} (\emph{nambikkai}) — \textquotedblleft{}trust\textquotedblright{}.

Trust, and the confidence that comes with it. All three are off the same old stem: Kannada \ka{ನಂಬಿಕೆ} (\emph{nambike}), Telugu \te{నమ్మకం} (\emph{nammakaṁ}), Tamil \ta{நம்பிக்கை}.

A \ta{விருந்தாளி} is given this before anything else is given, which is the whole of what a Tamil house means by hospitality.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Four.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{nambikkai}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{nambikkai}, then \emph{viruntāḷi}, and say who is given which
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{நம்பிக்கை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}trust\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[paṇivu]{\ta{பணிவு} (paṇivu) — humility}

\label{lesson:TA-C63-humility}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{nambikkai} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பணிவு}}
\textbf{\ta{பணிவு}} (\emph{paṇivu}) — \textquotedblleft{}humility\textquotedblright{}.

The bending: humility, deference, a manner rather than an act. Set it against \ta{மரியாதை}, which you already have — \ta{மரியாதை} is respect paid outward to somebody, \ta{பணிவு} is the carriage you keep in yourself.

Telugu's \te{మర్యాద} (\emph{maryāda}) is the same word as your \ta{மரியாதை}, which makes the pair easy to keep straight across the two.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Five, and the run is closed: a request, permission, hesitancy, trust, and humility.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{paṇivu}
  \item it once more, slowly
  \item all five in order — \emph{vēṇḍukōḷ}, \emph{aṉumati}, \emph{tayakkam}, \emph{nambikkai}, \emph{paṇivu}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{பணிவு} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}humility\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
